# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**Governing Policy:** Cigna CMM-311 Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 (Partial Knee Replacement section), effective 2026-08-04
https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-311%20Knee%20Replac%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

**Member:** Reese Mercado
**Member ID:** W529317483
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Arizona
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-01
**Reference number:** POC-8AD74FF769-66861
**Procedure:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), described in the notice dated 2026-08-01 (reference number POC-8AD74FF769-66861). The denial letter states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I am asking that this decision be reconsidered. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the records already in your file meet the plan's own published criteria.

## The Plan's Criteria and My Records

The policy states that "unicompartmental replacement is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

The three required elements are stated as: "◦ function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) ◦ loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration ◦ Criteria exception:"

Here is how my record maps to each of these:

**1. Function-limiting pain / loss of knee function affecting daily activities.**
My chart documents that I cannot climb stairs without assistance and wake 3-4 times nightly because of pain. This is the kind of loss of function the policy describes as interfering with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living. [If a specific walking-distance limitation was also documented by Dr. Lindqvist, please insert it here, e.g., "unable to walk more than ___ before pain limits activity."]

**2. Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three months.**
My records show:
- NSAIDs for 8 months (longer than the 3-month period referenced in the policy), with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-18, giving only about 3 weeks of partial relief.
- Supervised physical therapy for quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, 24 visits completed from 2026-05-12 to 2026-07-07, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

Taken together, this is more than three months of provider-directed, non-surgical treatment that did not resolve my symptoms.

**3. Imaging findings.**
The denial states that imaging does not support medical necessity. My MRI of the knee, dated 2026-06-08, documents full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. This is the same imaging that was part of the prior authorization submission, and I ask that it be reviewed again against the criteria quoted above.

**4. Non-indications.**
The policy also states that partial knee replacement "is considered not medically necessary for ANY other indication, condition, or when ANY of the following are present," but the denial notice does not identify which, if any, of those specific conditions the reviewer believed applied to me. I am not aware of any such condition in my history — I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, and my BMI is 29. If the denial was based on one of these non-indication criteria, I ask that the specific criterion be identified so that my surgeon and I can respond to it directly.

## What I Am Asking For

I am asking Cigna to reconsider this denial in light of the medical records already on file, which I believe show that the plan's own medical necessity criteria for unicompartmental (partial) knee replacement have been met. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary based on my exam findings, imaging, and 24 months of progressive symptoms that have not improved with conservative treatment.

Please treat this letter as my formal request for appeal. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-28, though I recognize the letter accompanying this denial is the authoritative source for that deadline and the correct mailing address. I am also submitting this appeal through my.cigna.com and am available by phone at 1-800-244-6224 if any additional information is needed.

Please send your written decision, and any further instructions for review, to the address below.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

________________________________
Reese Mercado
Member ID: W529317483
Address: [insert mailing address]
Phone: [insert phone number]
Date: [insert date of signing]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
